requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is enabled on node1.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled, the permanent and runtime rules matched, and the service plus rules recovered after node1 reboot with a changed boot identity.

requirements.requirement: SSH to node1 is allowed without source-address restriction.
requirements.summary: The active public zone retained its unrestricted SSH service, sshd listened on IPv4 and IPv6, and successful SSH banners were observed from both node2 and node3 before and after the reboot sequence.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is allowed only from node2 and rejected from node3 and all other sources, persistently.
requirements.summary: The permanent policy contains a higher-priority accept for node2's IPv4 address and a catch-all TCP/9000 reject. With a confirmed listener, node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 was rejected. The same rules and behavior were directly re-observed after node1 reboot and again after all node restarts.

requirements.requirement: The installed operating-system release and kernel are retained, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after execution. The implementation used the already-installed, active firewalld facility, with no package or kernel replacement and with final package health intact.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a reboot-persistent firewalld policy that preserves unrestricted SSH, permits TCP/9000 from node2, and rejects other sources; direct tests from node2 and node3 passed both before and after restart. The operating-system release and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol was coherently completed and independently corroborated for all managed nodes.
limitations: The universal “everywhere else” behavior was not probed from an arbitrary fourth source; it is supported by the observed catch-all reject rule plus a direct negative test from node3.

Node2 and node3 have no task-defined application data or cluster membership to validate after restart; their recovery evidence therefore covers applicable system, address, SSH, failed-unit, and socket state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The permanent firewall-rule additions and reload directly implemented the task. Temporary TCP/9000 listeners and test files were bounded verification prerequisites and were removed after each test, including the final cleanup. The three reboots served the mandatory provider-wide restart protocol. Final snapshots show no test listener or artifact, no failed services, and healthy package state. Each node has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered SSH/address/system state; node1 additionally has direct recovered firewall policy and traffic behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate all three restarts.
